title: Datum — Parametric Sketch Solver
description: An interactive geometric constraint solver in the spirit of Sutherland's Sketchpad. Sketch points, lines, circles AND circular arcs, then pin them together with real relations — coincident, horizontal/vertical, parallel, perpendicular, equal, tangent (line-to-arc and arc-to-arc), concentric, point-on-line/circle/arc, symmetric, colinear, midpoint, plus dimensional distance / angle / radius / diameter. Arcs are first-class: an arc reduces to a center, two endpoint points and a radius, held together by two intrinsic endpoint-on-circle residuals, so EVERY circle relation (radius, diameter, equal-radius, concentric, tangent, point-on) applies to arcs unchanged — draw one with a three-click center→start→end tool, drag it live, or flip its minor/major sweep. Every relation becomes a scalar residual equation and the whole system is driven to zero by a from-scratch Levenberg–Marquardt least-squares solver. The Jacobian is EXACT: each residual is written once over an abstract arithmetic and re-run through a sparse forward-mode dual number, so the derivative is the residual code differentiated by the compiler — one source of truth, no finite-difference noise (a live differential test confirms it matches central differences to ~1e-8, arc residuals included). Drag any point and the sketch re-solves live under your cursor; a Jacobian-rank degree-of-freedom analysis reports in real time whether the sketch is under-, well-, or over-constrained, and conflict diagnosis row-reduces the Jacobian to flag the SPECIFIC redundant constraints in red. One-click auto-constrain infers horizontal/vertical/parallel/perpendicular/equal/coincident from a rough drawing — admitting each only if it raises the rank, so it never over-constrains. Full undo/redo, save/open as JSON, and a shareable URL that reconstructs the whole sketch; double-click any dimension to retarget it. Eleven worked examples DRIVE live, including the Peaucellier–Lipkin inversor (1864) that traces a mathematically EXACT straight line (held to ~1e-12 across its sweep), Hoeken's approximate four-bar for contrast, and three arc showcases — a rounded slot, a tangent-arc fillet and a rounded rectangle, each fully constrained by one radius. A 22-check live self-test suite re-derives every claim from an independent reference.
